title: Call one body twice
starter:
%x = param 0 dtype=i32
%y = param 1 dtype=i32
# define a body %sq that squares ITS param 0, then call it on %x and on %y
%out = add %x %y
hints: A body is just a graph that uses params. Inside a body, `param 0` means whatever that call passes first.
Define `%sq = mul %p %p`, where `%p = param 0 dtype=i32`. That is the same node as `%x`, and that is fine.
Call it twice, `call %sq %x` and `call %sq %y`, then add the two results.

answer.code:
%x = param 0 dtype=i32
%y = param 1 dtype=i32
%p = param 0 dtype=i32
%sq = mul %p %p
%a = call %sq %x
%b = call %sq %y
%out = add %a %b
answer.explain: One body `mul p0 p0` is called twice with different args. Each call binds its own `param 0`, so the shared body (even though hash consing makes `%p` and `%x` the same node) computes `x*x` and `y*y` separately. Both products wrap like any i32 mul.
